definitions.gloss: edge of eaves; under the eaves
definitions.explanation: the area just outside a building, under the overhang of the roof
the front of a shop, often where goods are displayed

examples.japanese: {軒先|のきさき}で{雨宿|あまやど}りした。
examples.english: I took shelter from the rain under the eaves.

examples.japanese: {軒先|のきさき}に{風鈴|ふうりん}が{下|さ}がっている。
examples.english: A wind chime is hanging from the eaves.

examples.japanese: ツバメが{軒先|のきさき}に{巣|す}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: A swallow built a nest under the eaves.

examples.japanese: {軒先|のきさき}に{野菜|やさい}を{並|なら}べて{売|う}っている。
examples.english: They're selling vegetables displayed in front of the shop.

examples.japanese: {軒先|のきさき}に{看板|かんばん}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I put out a sign in front of the shop.

examples.japanese: {軒先|のきさき}{販売|はんばい}で{新鮮|しんせん}な{魚|さかな}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought fresh fish sold at the storefront.

notes:
Refers to the area just in front of a building, under the overhang of the roof. Also used for the front of a shop where goods are displayed.

WORD FORMATION:
{軒|のき} (eaves) + {先|さき} (tip, front)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {軒先|のきさき}で{雨宿|あまやど}りする: to take shelter from rain under the eaves
- {軒先|のきさき}に{並|なら}べる: to display/line up in front of a shop
- {軒先|のきさき}{販売|はんばい}: storefront sales

IDIOM:
{軒先|のきさき}を{貸|か}して{母屋|おもや}を{取|と}られる: lend the eaves and lose the main house (give an inch and they'll take a mile)

RELATED WORDS:
- {軒|のき}: eaves
- {庇|ひさし}: canopy, awning
- {店頭|てんとう}: in front of a store (formal)
- {店先|みせさき}: shopfront
